chapter.name: Arjuna Vishada Yoga
chapter.description: The prelude to the epic dialogue between Lord Krishna and Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra
chapter.theme: Arjuna's moral and emotional crisis before the battle

verses.speaker: Dhritarashtra
verses.sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच | धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः | मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ||
verses.transliteration: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca | dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ | māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāścaiva kimakurvata sañjaya ||
verses.englishTranslation: Dhritarashtra said: O Sanjay, assembled in the holy land of Kurukshetra and desirous of battle, what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do?
verses.meaning: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya about what his sons and the Pandavas did when they assembled for battle on the sacred field of Kurukshetra.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच | दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा | आचार्यमुपसङ्गम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत् ||
verses.transliteration: sañjaya uvāca | dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṃ vyūḍhaṃ duryodhanastadā | ācāryamupasaṅgamya rājā vacanamabravīt ||
verses.englishTranslation: Sanjay said: Observing the Pandava army arranged for battle, King Duryodhana approached his teacher and spoke these words.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya begins his narration by describing how Duryodhana approached his teacher after seeing the Pandava army arranged in formation.

verses.speaker: Duryodhana
verses.sanskrit: पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम् | व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता ||
verses.transliteration: paśyaitāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāmācārya mahatīṃ chamūm | vyūḍhāṃ drupadaputreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā ||
verses.englishTranslation: Behold, O Teacher, this mighty army of the sons of Pandu, arrayed by your wise disciple, the son of Drupada.
verses.meaning: Duryodhana draws Dronacharya's attention to the impressive military formation of the Pandavas arranged by Dhrishtadyumna, the son of Drupada.

verses.speaker: Duryodhana
verses.sanskrit: अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि | युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः ||
verses.transliteration: atra śūrā maheṣvāsā bhīmārjunasamā yudhi | yuyudhāno virāṭaśca drupadaśca mahārathaḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: Here are mighty bowmen equal to Bhima and Arjuna in battle - Yuyudhana, Virata, and the great warrior Drupada.
verses.meaning: Duryodhana lists the skilled warriors on the Pandava side who possess great strength and archery skills.

verses.speaker: Duryodhana
verses.sanskrit: धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान् | पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुंगवः ||
verses.transliteration: dhṛṣṭaketuścekitānaḥ kāśirājaśca vīryavān | purujitkuntibhojaśca śaibyaśca narapuṃgavaḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: Dhrishtaketu, Cekitana, the valiant King of Kashi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya the best of men.
verses.meaning: Duryodhana continues listing more mighty warriors and kings among the Pandava forces.

verses.speaker: Duryodhana
verses.sanskrit: युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान् | सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः ||
verses.transliteration: yudhāmanyuśca vikrānta uttamaujāśca vīryavān | saubhadro draupadeyāśca sarva eva mahārathāḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: Yudhamanyu the courageous, Uttamaujas the powerful, Subhadra's son, and the sons of Draupadi - all are great warriors.
verses.meaning: Duryodhana mentions more of the Pandava army including Abhimanyu (Subhadra's son) and the five sons of Draupadi.

verses.speaker: Duryodhana
verses.sanskrit: अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजसत्तम | नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते ||
verses.transliteration: asmākaṃ tu viśiṣṭā ye tānnibudha dvijasat́tama | nāykā mama sainysya | samjñārthaṃ tānbravīmi te ||
verses.englishTranslation: But listen, O best of the twice-born, to the names of our distinguished commanders - I shall name them to make you know.
verses.meaning: Duryodhana now turns to describe the commanders of his own army to impress Drona with the strength of his forces.

verses.speaker: Duryodhana
verses.sanskrit: भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिञ्जयः | अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिस्तथैव च ||
verses.transliteration: bhavānbhīṣmaśca karṇaśca kṛpaśca samitijñayaḥ | aśvatthāmā vikarṇaśca saumadatistathāiva ca ||
verses.englishTranslation: Yourself, Bhishma, Karna, Kripa - the victor in battles, Ashwatthama, Vikarna, and also Somadatta.
verses.meaning: Duryodhana lists the commanders of his own army including his uncle Bhishma, Karna, Drona, and others.

verses.speaker: Duryodhana
verses.sanskrit: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः | नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः ||
verses.transliteration: anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ | nānāśastrapraharaṇāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: There are many other brave warriors ready to die for me, armed with various weapons and all experienced in warfare.
verses.meaning: Duryodhana emphasizes that his army has many other skilled warriors dedicated to his cause.

verses.speaker: Duryodhana
verses.sanskrit: अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्मा भिरक्षितम् | पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमा भिरक्षितम् ||
verses.transliteration: aparyāptaṃ tadasmākaṃ balaṃ bhīṣmā bhirakṣitam | paryāptaṃ tvidemet́eṣāṃ balaṃ bhīmā bhirakṣitam ||
verses.englishTranslation: Our army protected by Bhishma is unlimited, while the army of the Pandavas protected by Bhima is limited.
verses.meaning: Duryodhana expresses confidence that his forces under Bhishma are far superior to the Pandava forces.

verses.speaker: Duryodhana
verses.sanskrit: अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः | भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि ||
verses.transliteration: ayaneṣu ca sarveṣu yathābhāgamavasthatāḥ | bhīṣmamevābhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi ||
verses.englishTranslation: Therefore, all of you stationed at your respective positions on all fronts, protect Bhishma with all your might.
verses.meaning: Duryodhana instructs his commanders to position themselves strategically and provide strong defense at all points, especially to protect Bhishma.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: तस्य सञ्जनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः | सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान् ||
verses.transliteration: tasya sañjanayan harṣaṃ kuruvṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ | siṃhanādaṃ vinadyoccaiḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān ||
verses.englishTranslation: To inspire Duryodhana, the great Kaurava patriarch Bhishma, roaring like a lion, blew his conch shell loudly and powerfully.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya describes how Bhishma, the elder of the Kaurava clan, boosted Duryodhana's morale by sounding his conch with a mighty roar.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: तत:  शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः | सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलो अभवत् ||
verses.transliteration: tataḥ śaṅkhāśca bheryaśca paṇavānakagomukhāḥ | sahasaivābhyahanyanta sa śabdastumuló abhavat ||
verses.englishTranslation: Thereupon, conches, kettledrums, cymbals, and war horns sounded simultaneously, and the sound was tumultuous.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya describes the grand military display as various musical instruments of war are sounded together, creating a tremendous noise.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: तत: श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ | माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः ||
verses.transliteration: tataḥ śvetairhayairyukte mahati syandane sthitau | mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaścaiva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: Then Lord Krishna and Arjuna, seated in their magnificent chariot drawn by white horses, blew their divine conches.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya describes the divine chariot of Krishna and Arjuna, drawn by white horses, from which they sound their conches.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनञ्जयः | पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः ||
verses.transliteration: pāñchajanyaṃ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṃ dhana janyaḥ | pauṇḍraṃ dadhmau mahāśaṅkhaṃ bhīmakaramā vṛkodraḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: Lord Krishna blew his conch Panchjanya, Arjuna blew his conch Devadatta, and Bhima blew the great conch Paundra.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya details which famous Pandava leader sounded which conch - Krishna with Panchjanya, Arjuna with Devadatta, and Bhima with Paundra.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः | नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ ||
verses.transliteration: anantavijayaṃ rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ | nakulaḥ sahadevaśca sughośamaṇipuṣpakau ||
verses.englishTranslation: King Yudhishthira blew his conch Anantavijaya, while Nakul and Sahadeva blew their conches Sughosh and Manipushpak.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya describes the conches blown by the other Pandava leaders including the Pandava king Yudhishthira and his brothers.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः | धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः ||
verses.transliteration: kāśyaśca parameṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ | dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaśca sātyakiścāparājitaḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: The King of Kashi, the great warrior Shikhandi, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and the invincible Satyaki also blew their conches.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya continues listing other important Pandava allies who sounded their conches.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते | सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्ददध्मु पृथक् पृथक् ||
verses.transliteration: drupado draupadeyāśca sarvaśaḥ pṛthivīpate | saubhradaśca mahābāhuḥ śaṅkhānda dadhaṃ pṛthak pṛthak ||
verses.englishTranslation: O King, Drupada and his sons, and the mighty-armed Abhimanyu, all sounded their respective conches separately.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya describes how Drupada, the father of Draupadi, his grandsons (the Pandavas' children), and Abhimanyu each sounded their conches.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत् | नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलो व्यनुनादयन् ||
verses.transliteration: sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ hṛdayāni vyadārayat | nabhśca pṛthivīṃ caiva tumulo vyanunādin ||
verses.englishTranslation: That tumultuous sound pierced the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons and reverberated through the earth and sky.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya describes the effect of this great sound on Duryodhana's forces - it terrified them as it echoed across land and sky.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: अथ व्यवस्थितान्दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः | प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ||
verses.transliteration: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ | pravṛtte śastrasampāte dhanurut́yamya pāṇḍavaḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: Seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra standing arrayed, and when the shower of arrows had begun, Arjuna whose flag bore the emblem of the monkey took up his bow.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya describes how Arjuna, seeing the Kaurava army arranged and ready for battle, picked up his bow to begin the fight.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: तत:  शंकरं भगवान् वाक्यं इदं अब्रवीत् | प्रेक्ष्य पाण्डवानीकंव्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा ||
verses.transliteration: tataḥ śaṅkaraṃ bhagavān vākyaṃ idaṃ abravīt | prekṣya pāṇḍavānīkam vyūḍhaṃ duryodhanastadā ||
verses.englishTranslation: The Lord spoke to Arjuna after observing the Pandava army arrayed for battle.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya introduces Krishna's intervention by noting that the Lord observed the armies and prepared to speak to Arjuna.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेच्युत ||
verses.transliteration: arjuna uvāca | senayorubhayormadhye rathaṃ sthāpaya mechyuta ||
verses.englishTranslation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, place my chariot between the two armies so that I can observe these warriors who desire to fight.
verses.meaning: Arjuna requests Krishna to position the chariot in the middle of the battlefield so he can examine both armies before the battle begins.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्धुकामानवस्थितान् | कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन्रणसमुद्यमे ||
verses.transliteration: yāvadetiān nirīkṣe'haṃ yoddhukāmānavasthitān | kair maya saha yoddhavyamasmín raṇasamudyame ||
verses.englishTranslation: I wish to see those who desire to fight me and are here for battle.  I want to know with whom I have to engage in this struggle.
verses.meaning: Arjuna expresses his desire to survey the warriors before engaging in battle.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत | सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम् ||
verses.transliteration: evamukto hṛṣīkeśo gudākeśena bhārata | senayorubhayormadhye sthāpayitvā rathottamam ||
verses.englishTranslation: Thus addressed by Arjuna, O Bharat, Krishna placed the magnificent chariot between the two armies.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya describes how Krishna complies with Arjuna's request and positions the chariot between the armies.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम् | उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरून्इति ||
verses.transliteration: bhīṣmadroṇapramukhataḥ sarveṣāṃ ca mahīkṣitām | uvāca pārtha paśyaitān samavitān kurūn iti ||
verses.englishTranslation: In front of Bhishma, Drona and all the other kings of the earth, Krishna said to Arjuna: 'O Partha, see how the Kurus are assembled.'
verses.meaning: Sanjaya describes Krishna pointing out the Kaurava forces to Arjuna, with all the great generals and kings visible.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितृन्अथ पितामहान् | आच���र्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातृन्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा ||
verses.transliteration: tatrāpaśyat sthitān pārthaḥ pitṛn atha pitāmahān | āchāryān mātulan bhrātṛn putrān pautrān sakhīns tathā ||
verses.englishTranslation: Arjuna saw arrayed there his fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons and friends.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya describes how Arjuna saw all his relatives and friends standing in the enemy formation, which causes his emotional disturbance.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: सौहृदान्सर्वान्पश्यन्स कृपया परयाविष्टः | दुःखितो विषीदन्नइदं वचनमब्रवीत् ||
verses.transliteration: sauhṛdān sarvān paśyan sa kṛpayā parayāviṣṭḥ | duḥkhito viṣīdann idaṃ vacanamabravīt ||
verses.englishTranslation: Seeing all his friends and relatives assembled, Arjuna was overwhelmed with great pity and spoke despondently.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya describes Arjuna's emotional breakdown upon seeing his loved ones arrayed as enemies.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण यायातो व्यथितं मनः ||
verses.transliteration: arjuna uvāca | dṛṣṭvemam svajanaṃ kṛṣṇa yāyāto vyathitaṃ manaḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, seeing my kinsmen arrayed for battle, I feel my limbs quail, my mouth is parched.
verses.meaning: Arjuna expresses his physical and emotional distress at the prospect of fighting his own family members.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते | गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते ||
verses.transliteration: vepathuśca śarīre me romaharsaśca jāyate | gāṇḍīvaṃ sraṃsate hastāt tvacaiva paridahyate ||
verses.englishTranslation: My body quivers, my hair stands on end, my Gandiva bow slips from my hand, and my skin is burning.
verses.meaning: Arjuna describes his physical symptoms of extreme distress - trembling, hair standing on end, losing grip on his bow, and burning sensation on his skin.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः | निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव ||
verses.transliteration: na ca śaknomyavasthātuṃ bhramtīva ca me manaḥ | nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava ||
verses.englishTranslation: I cannot stand firm, my mind is reeling, and O Krishna, I see omens that are all unfavorable.
verses.meaning: Arjuna expresses his inability to stand and his seeing of bad omens for the battle ahead.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: न कामये विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च | किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीविताय वा ||
verses.transliteration: na kāmaye vijayaṃ kṛṣṇa na ca rājyaṃ sukhāni ca | kiṃ no rājyena govinda kiṃ bhogairjīvitāya vā ||
verses.englishTranslation: I do not desire victory, O Krishna, nor kingdom nor pleasures.  What use is a kingdom to us, or enjoyments or even life itself?
verses.meaning: Arjuna questions the purpose of fighting for kingdom and pleasure when it involves killing his own relatives.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च | त इमे अवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च ||
verses.transliteration: yeṣāmarthe kāṅkṣitaṃ no rājyaṃ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca | ta ime avasthitā yudhe prāṇāṃs tyaktvā dhanāni ca ||
verses.englishTranslation: For the sake of whom we desired this kingdom and its pleasures, they stand here in battle having forsaken life and wealth.
verses.meaning: Arjuna points out the irony that those for whom they fought for kingdom and pleasures are now ready to sacrifice their lives.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: आचार्याः पितरः पुत्राः तथैव च पितामहाः | मातुलाः श्वशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः समृते परः ||
verses.transliteration: ācāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrāḥ tathāiva ca pitāmahāḥ | mātulaḥ śvaśurāḥ pautrāḥ śyālāḥ samṛte paraḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: Here are teachers, fathers, sons, and also grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and relatives.
verses.meaning: Arjuna lists all the family relations present in the enemy army, emphasizing the bonds of kinship he would break by fighting.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: न कृत्वा रक्षणं हन्स्यामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन | इह लोके परलोके च न मे श्रेयः स्याद् उभयोः ||
verses.transliteration: na kṛtvā rakṣaṇaṃ hanyāmi ghnato'pi madhusūdana | iha loke paraloke ca na me śreyaḥ syād ubhayoḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: Even if they kill me, O Madhusudana, I shall not kill them. This brings me no good in this world or hereafter.
verses.meaning: Arjuna declares that he will not kill even if killed in return, as it serves no purpose in this world or the next.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: किं घ्नता प्राप्स्यामहं कृष्ण न त्वेव स्यादुपप्लुतम् | निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याद्जनार्दन ||
verses.transliteration: kiṃ ghnātā prāpsyāmahaṃ kṛṣṇa na tveva syādupaplyutam | nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrān naḥ kā prītiḥ syāj janārdana ||
verses.englishTranslation: What good can come from killing the sons of Dhritarashtra, O Krishna? How can we be happy after slaying them?
verses.meaning: Arjuna questions the benefit of killing the Kauravas and achieving victory when it will only bring sorrow.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः | कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadvyapyete na paśyanti lobhophatacetasaḥ | kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ mitradrohe ca pātakam ||
verses.englishTranslation: Though they, blinded by greed, see no sin in destroying the family and no wrong in betraying friends, how can we fail to see the evil in this?
verses.meaning: Arjuna argues that even though the Kauravas don't recognize the sin of family destruction and treachery, Krishna and he should understand these wrongs.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः | धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत ||
verses.transliteration: kulakṣaye praṇaśyanti kuladharmāḥ sanātanāḥ | dharme naṣṭe kulaṃ kṛtsnam adharmó abhibhavty uta ||
verses.englishTranslation: With the destruction of family, the eternal family traditions are destroyed, and when righteousness is ruined, unrighteousness prevails.
verses.meaning: Arjuna explains that the destruction of family leads to the destruction of eternal dharma (righteousness) and the rise of adharma (unrighteousness).

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः | स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः ||
verses.transliteration: adharmābhibhavāt kṛṣṇa pradushyanti kulastriyaḥ | strīṣu dustāsu vārṣṇeya jāyate varṇasaṅkaraḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: When unrighteousness prevails, O Krishna, the women of the family become corrupt, and from the corruption of women, O Vrisni, comes confusion of castes.
verses.meaning: Arjuna describes the social consequences of unrighteousness - the corruption of women and the resulting confusion of family lineages.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च | पतन्ति पितरो ह्यर्षहि पिण्डोदकक्रियाविः ||
verses.transliteration: saṅkaro narakāyaiva kulaghnānāṃ kulasya ca | patanti pitaro hyarsahi piṇḍodakakriyāviḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: Caste confusion brings hell to the family and to those who destroy the family.  The ancestors fall from grace lacking the offerings of rice and water.
verses.meaning: Arjuna explains the spiritual consequences - caste confusion leads to hell, and ancestors lose their peace without proper funeral rites.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः | उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः ||
verses.transliteration: doṣair etaiḥ kulaghnānāṃ varṇasaṅkarakārakaiḥ | utsādyante jātidharmāḥ kuladharmāśca śāśvatāḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: By these evil deeds of the family-slayers, which lead to confusion of castes, the eternal laws of family and caste are destroyed.
verses.meaning: Arjuna emphasizes that family destruction causes the permanent loss of eternal family and social laws.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन | नरकेऽनियतः कालो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम ||
verses.transliteration: utsannakuladharmāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ janārdana | narke'niyataḥ kālo bhavatītyanuśuśruma ||
verses.englishTranslation: O Janardana, we have heard that those men of a destroyed family dwell in hell for an indefinite period.
verses.meaning: Arjuna references the scriptures that say those responsible for family destruction go to hell for an indefinite time.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम् | यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः ||
verses.transliteration: aho bata mahat pāpaṃ kartuṃ vyavasitā vayam | yad rājyasukhalobhena hantuṃ svajanam udyatāḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: Alas!  We have resolved to commit a great sin - driven by desire for kingdom and pleasures to kill our own relatives.
verses.meaning: Arjuna expresses dismay at the graveness of the sin he and the Pandavas are about to commit.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit: यदि माम् अप्रतीकारम् अशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः | धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युः तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् ||
verses.transliteration: yadi mām apratīkāram aśastram śastrapāṇayaḥ | dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyuḥ tanme kṣemataraṃ bhavet ||
verses.englishTranslation: Better would it be if the armed sons of Dhritarashtra killed me in battle while I remain unresisting and unarmed.
verses.meaning: Arjuna expresses his preference to be killed without fighting rather than to kill his own kinsmen.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वार्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् | विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ||
verses.transliteration: evam uktvārjunaḥ samkhye rathopastha upāviśat | visṛjya śaśaraṃ cāpaṃ śokasaṃvignamānasaḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: Having thus spoken in the battle, Arjuna sat down on the chariot, his mind overpowered by sorrow, casting aside his bow and arrows.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya describes how Arjuna, overwhelmed with grief, puts down his bow and sits in the chariot, unable to continue the battle.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: तं तथा कृपयाविष्टम् अश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम् | विषीदन्तं इदं वाक्यं उवाच मधुसूदनः ||
verses.transliteration: taṃ tathā kṛpayāviṣṭam aśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam | viṣīdantaṃ idaṃ vākyaṃ uvāca madhusūdanaḥ ||
verses.englishTranslation: Upon seeing Arjuna full of compassion, overwhelmed with sorrow, his eyes filled with tears, Krishna spoke to him these words.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya describes how Krishna observes Arjuna's despair and decides to address him, which marks the beginning of Krishna's teachings.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit: भगवान् उवाच | कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् | अनार्यजुष्टम् अस्वर्ग्यम् अकीर्तिकरम् अर्जुन ||
verses.transliteration: bhagavān uvāca | kutastv kāśmalam idaṃ viṣame samupasthitam | anāryajuṣṭam asvargyam akīrtikaram arjuna ||
verses.englishTranslation: The Blessed Lord said:  Arjuna, how has this delusion come upon you in this hour of crisis? This is not the path of the noble; it does not lead to heaven and brings infamy.
verses.meaning: Krishna begins his teaching by questioning Arjuna's weakness and reminding him of his duty as a warrior, setting up for the deeper teachings to come.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.sanskrit: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते | क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परंतप ||
verses.transliteration: klaibyaṃ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitat tvayy upapadyate | kṣudraṃ hṛdayadaurbalyaṃ tyaktvottiṣṭha parantapa ||
verses.englishTranslation: Do not yield to cowardice, O Partha. This does not become you. Rise up and shake off this petty weakness of heart.  Arise, O vanquisher of enemies!
verses.meaning: Krishna concludes Chapter 1 with a powerful call to action, urging Arjuna to abandon his weaknesses and remember his warrior duty, leading into Chapter 2's teachings.
